2026-08-19T12:31:06.1966341Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-19T12:31:06.1966877Z 
2026-08-19T12:31:06.1967307Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-19T12:31:06.1967997Z 
2026-08-19T12:31:06.1968517Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-19T12:31:06.1969253Z 
2026-08-19T12:31:06.1972310Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-19T12:31:06.1983371Z >
2026-08-19T12:31:06.1995821Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2000467Z >
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2001615Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2002824Z 
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2003012Z ### How to Use
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2003285Z 
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2004613Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2005736Z 
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2005913Z ```bash
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2006895Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2007914Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2008712Z ```
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2008940Z 
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2009238Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2009905Z ```bash
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2010578Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2011682Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2012868Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2013942Z ```
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2014168Z 
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2015069Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2016541Z ```bash
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2017256Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2018185Z ```
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2018414Z 
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2018803Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2019837Z ```bash
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2022812Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2024169Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2025145Z ```
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2025373Z 
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2025720Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2026632Z 
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2029009Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2031689Z 
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2031873Z ```bash
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2032393Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2033603Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2034787Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2035213Z 
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2035924Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2037655Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2038834Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2039404Z ```
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2039640Z 
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2040817Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2042274Z 
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2042452Z ```bash
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2043344Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2044579Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2045555Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2046364Z 
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2046936Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2048093Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2048791Z ```
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2049019Z 
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2049259Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2050370Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2051791Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2053211Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2054684Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2056681Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2057516Z 
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2057694Z ### Notes
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2057942Z 
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2058896Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2061154Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2063077Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2064994Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2067056Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2068673Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2070097Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-19T12:31:06.2071056Z </mcp-clis>
